subject: how can i change the datetime scales in x axis?

messages.author: 76e101ce83bfedbb
messages.subject: how can i change the datetime scales in x axis?
parts:
hi all, 

i want to change the datetime scales in x axis using the function scale_datetime() but this function doesn't work in my example

could you help me?

* i also  want change the colors for the factor according to the colors in the legend is possible in ggvis?

SERVER.R

master<-NULL
master$x<- rep(seq(as.POSIXct("2011-01-10 00:01:00"),as.POSIXct("2011-01-10 00:30:00"),"mins"),3)
master$y<- rep(c("a","b","c"),30)
master$factor<-rep(c("red","blue","yellow"),30)

master<-as.data.frame(master)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
master$id<-seq_len(nrow(master))
  
lb <- linked_brush(keys = master$id, "red")
master%>%ggvis(~factor(x),~y,fill=~factor ) %>%
layer_rects(width = band(), height = band(), fill.brush := "red", opacity := 0.3) %>%
scale_datetime("x",nice="minute")%>% lb$input() %>%
scale_nominal("y", padding = 0, points = FALSE) %>% bind_shiny("plot1")


selected <- lb$selected
  
        
  master_selected <- reactive({
    master[selected(), ]
  })
  
  
output$hhh<-renderTable({return(master_selected())})
output$j<-renderText({as.character(master_selected()$factor[1])})
})

UI.R

library("ggvis")
shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
  ggvisOutput("plot1"),

  tableOutput("hhh"),
  textOutput("j")
))

Thanks for your help

Natalia

messages.subject: Re: how can i change the datetime scales in x axis?
parts:
Hi Natalia,

On your questions: 

My understanding is that scale_datetime() is a special case of a numerical scale; you have set a nominal scale for "x" by virtue of using ~factor(x). I think this is the source of the problem.

Would it work to keep the x-scale numeric and to specify the extent of the rectangle using the data:

master$x2 <- master$x + 60 # adds 60 seconds to x

then define the rectangles accordingly:

layer_rects(x2 = ~x2, height = band(), fill.brush := "red", opacity := 0.3)


For the fill colors to match the factor, something like this could work:      

scale_nominal("fill", domain = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), range = c("red", "yellow", "blue"))


all together:

    master %>% 
      ggvis(~x,~y,fill=~factor ) %>%
      layer_rects(x2 = ~x2, height = band(), fill.brush := "red", opacity := 0.3) %>%
      lb$input() %>%
      scale_nominal("fill", domain = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), range = c("red", "yellow", "blue")) %>%
